notes: The output row grain is one per Master SKU (12 rows); Stock supplies qty and must be joined to Master on Company + Item code, never on Item code alone, because item codes are unique only within a company (6 codes x 2 companies).
SKU is already a text composite (<Company>-<zero-padded item code>) in Master; take it from Master rather than rebuilding it from Stock so leading zeros survive.

Quantity pieces is already expressed in individual pieces as required by /qty; the sheet appears to hold a single stock figure per item, but if the workbook grows to multiple lots per company+item the qty must be summed as an additive aggregate rather than deduplicated.

tables.reason: Master sheet is a product master list: one row per item (12 rows, SKU unique 12/12), with SKU, company/brand prefix, a local item code that repeats once per company (6 distinct values, 2 rows each), and a description unique per row. It is the only table carrying product identity and names, and the operator states the Master SKU is the output identity.

columns.name: SKU
columns.reason: Column named SKU, 12 distinct values in 12 rows, formatted as <company>-<4-digit code> (TH-0001, MY-0003), matching the contract's unique SKU identifier; text values so leading zeros are preserved.

columns.name: Company
columns.reason: Two values (TH 6, MY 6) that exactly prefix the SKU values. It is the company scoping key that makes Item code unique; the contract has no company field, so it is used only as a join component, never as an output field.

columns.name: Item code
columns.reason: Values 0001–0006, 6 distinct with 2 rows each — i.e. unique only within Company, exactly as the operator warned. It repeats the numeric part of the SKU and is therefore a join key component, not an output identity.

columns.name: Description
columns.reason: Free-text item description, 12 distinct values in 12 rows, one per SKU (e.g. 'TH item 1'); this is the only column in the workbook that can supply the required product_name.

tables.reason: Stock sheet holds no product identity or text attributes, only Company + Item code + a numeric quantity column (11–166, 12 distinct values, no nulls) — a stock-on-hand/lot table for the 12 items of Master. Its key is the pair Company + Item code, since Item code alone repeats across the two companies.

columns.name: Company
columns.reason: Same two-value company domain (MY 6, TH 6) as Master; needed to scope Item code before matching to the Master SKU. Not an output field in the contract.

columns.name: Item code
columns.reason: Values 0001–0006 with 2 rows each, mirroring Master's local item codes; it is the join component to Master together with Company and must not be matched across companies.

columns.name: Quantity pieces
columns.reason: Only measure column in the stock sheet, fully populated integers from 11 to 166; the header states the unit is pieces, which matches the contract's '/qty' description ('stock in individual pieces'), so no unit conversion is required.

changes_from_draft: Kept /sku from Master.SKU so the output identity preserves original text and leading zeros.
Added the Stock source and a left join from products to stock on Company + Item code; this respects the rule that item codes are unique only within a company.
Mapped /product_name from Master.Description, the only product-name column.
Mapped /qty directly from Stock.Quantity pieces; the header already states pieces, so no unit conversion or rounding was added.
Set record dedupe keys to /sku to keep one target record per Master SKU.
Set attributes_passthrough=false because the target schema has additionalProperties=false and Company/Item code are join-only attributes.
